title: Finite exceptional operations and enriched adjunction on coherent coefficient systems
statement:
Fix the global finite-field datum $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$ of characteristic $p$ [def-weil-finite-field-fiber], a prime $\ell\ne p$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation ring $R$ and uniformizer $\varpi$, and put $A_n=R/\varpi^n$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $f:X\to Y$ be a separated finite-type morphism of separated finite-type $k$-schemes, and fix a compactification $f=pj$ with $j$ open and $p$ proper [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties, def-nagata-compactification]. For $W=X,Y$, use the category $\mathscr S_W$ of strict semilinear $((A_n)_W)_n$-module systems, its derived category, reduction functor $\mathcal R_W$, limit functor $\mathcal L_W$, and fiberwise internal and global mapping systems $\mathcal I_W,\mathcal H_W$ of [lem-coef-derived-system-evaluation-calculus]. Let $\mathscr N_W\subset D(\mathscr S_W)$ be the full subcategory of normalized systems whose every level lies in the finite-Tor constructible category $D^b_{ctf}(W,A_n)$ [def-coef-normalized-dvr-tower, def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude, def-weil-pbc-constructible-complexes, lem-sf-proetale-constructible-origin]. No bound independent of $n$ is required.

The finite functors $Rf_{!,n}=Rp_*j_!$ [def-weil-integral-rational-qbar-compact-support] and $Rf_n^!$ [def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image] admit functorial realizations $\mathcal F_f:\mathscr N_X\to\mathscr N_Y$ and $\mathcal E_f:\mathscr N_Y\to\mathscr N_X$ on these derived coefficient systems. Their evaluations, including quotient maps, are the finite operations and canonical coefficient-change maps. The integral compact-support functor, when defined as the total limit of finite compact supports, is $\mathcal L_Y\mathcal F_f\mathcal R_X$ as a functor, with its specified finite projections.

Normalize the coherent dualizing system by $\Omega_W=\mathcal E_{a_W}((A_n)_{\operatorname{Spec}k})_n$ for the structure morphism $a_W:W\to\operatorname{Spec}k$, with the same realization of the finite functors; its level $n$ is $\omega_{W,n}=Ra_{W,n}^!A_n$. Put $\mathcal D_W(M)=\mathcal I_W(M,\Omega_W)$. For $M\in\mathscr N_W$, this dual system belongs to $\mathscr N_W$. Then $\mathcal E_f\cong\mathcal D_Xf^*\mathcal D_Y$ is a natural isomorphism of derived coefficient-system functors, where $f^*$ is derived levelwise finite pullback [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom]. It is the tensor-Hom evaluation transpose defining the finite dual-formula maps of [lem-coef-finite-exceptional], formed on simultaneous system resolutions. It respects normalization and evaluation pairings as identities of system maps. The total limit of the chosen $\Omega_W$ is the dualizing construction of [prop-coef-integral-dualizing], with these same finite projections.

For $M\in\mathscr N_X$ and $N\in\mathscr N_Y$ there is a natural isomorphism in $D(\operatorname{Tow}(\operatorname{Ab}))$
$$\mathcal A_{M,N}:\mathcal H_Y(\mathcal F_fM,N)\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathcal H_X(M,\mathcal E_fN).$$
It is the fiberwise derived evaluation/counit transpose on simultaneous coefficient-system resolutions. Its evaluation at $n$ is the canonical finite enriched adjunction
$$R\operatorname{Hom}_{Y,A_n}(Rf_{!,n}M_n,N_n)\cong R\operatorname{Hom}_{X,A_n}(M_n,Rf_n^!N_n),$$
transported from the ordinary etale adjunction by the etale/pro-etale comparison [prop-asd-internal-adjunction, lem-sf-class-compact-support-comparison, thm-weil-pbc-site-comparison]. This specifies an actual natural transformation before total inverse limit, with its inverse and evaluation/transpose identities, not a lift characterized only by its evaluations. The system comparisons identify the finite units and counits with those of [lem-coef-finite-exceptional]. No integral exceptional functor, integral adjunction, integral constructibility or Tor bound is asserted.

source.place: Proof, finite dual formula and coefficient adjunction maps; simultaneous coherent refinement is an additional agent-formulated obligation. Resolution foundations: sites-cohomology.tex Tags 06YS (lemma-K-flat-resolution), 0A95 (lemma-RHom-well-defined), 0941 (lemma-derived-limit-is-ok); injectives.tex Tag 079P (theorem-K-injective-embedding-grothendieck). None of these tags alone states the coherent finite exceptional realization.

proof.text: For each $W=X,Y$, let $\mathscr S_W^{\mathrm{et}}$ be the Grothendieck abelian category of strict semilinear $((A_n)_W)_n$-module systems on the small étale site, and use its ordinary unbounded derived category. The coefficient-system theorem gives componentwise exact evaluations, joint detection of isomorphisms, normalized transitions, derived scalar extension, and the derived inverse-image/direct-image adjunctions on system categories. The open map $j$ acts by exact extension by zero on systems, while the proper map $p$ has a total derived direct image. The K-flat and right-derived-functor constructions make these actual triangulated functors and actual transformations on systems, so no family of unrelated finite-level maps is being lifted. The rings $A_n$ are finite by the DVR finite-quotient theorem, and $X,Y,\overline X$ are Noetherian by finite type over the field $k$; these verify the hypotheses of the ambient finite-coefficient results below.

source.place: Finite duality, coefficient-change compatibility, and enriched adjunction before total inverse limits.

proof.text: Define $F_f^{\mathrm{et}}=Rp_{*,\bullet}j_{!,\bullet}$ on $D(\mathscr S_X^{\mathrm{et}})$. It is exact and preserves arbitrary coproducts: $j_!$ is a left adjoint and hence preserves coproducts, the proper derived direct image preserves coproducts at every finite coefficient, and coproducts and evaluations of systems are componentwise. The coefficient-system comparison theorem transports these componentwise coproduct isomorphisms to an isomorphism of system maps. Thus $F_f^{\mathrm{et}}$ is an exact coproduct-preserving functor between derived categories of Grothendieck abelian categories.

source.place: Finite duality, coefficient-change compatibility, and enriched adjunction before total inverse limits.

proof.text: Use [lem-pur-etale-coefficient-system-adjoint] for this same $A_n=R/\varpi^n$, $f$ and compactification. It supplies the actual exact right adjoint $G_f^{\mathrm{et}}$ of $F_f^{\mathrm{et}}$ on the ordinary unbounded derived categories of strict systems, with its evaluated units, counits and transition mates. Its Brown construction is valid because the system categories are Grothendieck and Step 2 proves that $F_f^{\mathrm{et}}$ is exact and preserves coproducts. We choose this right adjoint, rather than reconstructing a functor from finite adjoints. Its unit $\eta$ and counit $\epsilon$ are transformations of system functors and satisfy the triangle identities there.

source.place: Finite duality, coefficient-change compatibility, and enriched adjunction before total inverse limits.

proof.text: Here is the projection input for evaluation. For the derived left adjoint $L_n$ to $e_n$, its level $q\le n$ is $-\otimes^L_{A_n}A_q$ and its higher levels are zero. The canonical map $L_nF_{f,n}^{\mathrm{et}}\to F_f^{\mathrm{et}}L_n$ is the proper projection map followed by the open tensor comparison. At $q\le n$ these maps are isomorphisms by [lem-amb-proper-coproducts-projection] with the constant $A_n$-module $A_q$ and [lem-pur-etale-open-derived-tensor]; both results allow unbounded complexes and impose no finite Tor dimension on $A_q/A_n$. Above $n$ both sides vanish. The system calculus constructs this map and evaluations detect its invertibility. Thus $F_f^{\mathrm{et}}L_n\cong L_nF_{f,n}^{\mathrm{et}}$. The adjunctions give $\operatorname{Hom}(K,e_nG_f^{\mathrm{et}}N)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(F_{f,n}^{\mathrm{et}}K,e_nN)$. Yoneda and counit-compatible uniqueness identify $e_nG_f^{\mathrm{et}}N$ with $f_n^\times N_n$, as in the system-adjoint theorem, with the evaluated counits.

source.place: Finite duality, coefficient-change compatibility, and enriched adjunction before total inverse limits.

proof.text: Write $V_W=\nu_{W,\bullet}^*$ and $U_W=R\nu_{W,\bullet,*}$ for the site-comparison adjunction on systems. The canonical unit $1\to U_WV_W$ is an isomorphism: its evaluations are the units of the unbounded fully faithful comparison. For any system whose levels have etale origin, the counit $V_WU_WM\to M$ is likewise invertible, by its evaluated counits and conservativity. This uses the unbounded comparison, not the bounded-below final clause of the coefficient-system theorem. Hence these are actual inverse equivalences on the full subcategory of systems with etale-origin levels. Unbounded direct-image comparison and open comparison give $V_YF_f^{\mathrm{et}}\cong Rp_{*,\bullet}j_{!,\bullet}V_X$ as actual maps. Transport the chosen adjunction through these equivalences. Every bounded constructible finite-coefficient level has etale origin, so this applies to the domains in the statement; no common lower bound in $n$ is used.

source.place: Finite duality, coefficient-change compatibility, and enriched adjunction before total inverse limits.

proof.text: Restrict the transferred compact-support functor to $\mathscr N_X$. At level $n$, extension by zero preserves constructibility and the proper direct-image bound preserves constructibility and finite Tor amplitude; a dimension bound for the compactification is supplied by finite type over $k$. The quotient transition is the composite of the finite compact-support coefficient comparison with the transition of the input system, and the restriction-of-scalars comparison composes for successive quotients. Hence $F_f:\mathscr N_X\to\mathscr N_Y$ is defined by actual system maps and agrees under evaluation with $Rf_{!,n}$, with the stated transitions. Its total limit is therefore the specified integral compact-support construction whenever that construction is defined.

source.place: Finite duality, coefficient-change compatibility, and enriched adjunction before total inverse limits.

proof.text:
The transition identification uses the system-adjoint theorem, which explicitly identifies the transitions of $G_f^{\mathrm{et}}$ with finite adjunction mates. To spell out that mate, write $T^W_{m,n}=-\otimes^L_{A_m}A_n$ and $q:T^Y_{m,n}F_{f,m}\cong F_{f,n}T^X_{m,n}$. If $t^N:T^Y_{m,n}N_m\to N_n$ is the transition-adjoint of $N$, the transition-adjoint $s$ of $G_fN$ is the $F_{f,n}\dashv G_{f,n}$ transpose of
$$F_{f,n}T^X_{m,n}G_{f,m}N_m\xrightarrow{q^{-1}}T^Y_{m,n}F_{f,m}G_{f,m}N_m\xrightarrow{T^Y_{m,n}\epsilon_{m,N_m}}T^Y_{m,n}N_m\xrightarrow{t^N}N_n.$$
The evaluation-left-adjoint theorem describes transitions as precomposition with its actual $\sigma_{m,n}$ maps, so this is the transition of the chosen system adjoint, not a newly assigned transition. The counit identity of [lem-coef-finite-exceptional] says that the transpose of $b_{m,n,N_m}$ is the first two arrows. Naturality of transposition therefore gives
$$s=G_{f,n}(t^N)\circ b_{m,n,N_m}.$$
Counit-compatible uniqueness identifies the chosen finite adjoints with the specified $Rf_n^!$.

source.place: Finite duality, coefficient-change compatibility, and enriched adjunction before total inverse limits.

proof.text: The finite exceptional theorem makes every $b_{m,n}$ invertible and gives its quotient cocycle together with the unit and counit compatibility equations. The finite preservation theorem keeps $G_{f,n}$ inside $D^b_{ctf}$. Consequently the Brown right adjoint restricts to a functor $\mathcal E_f:\mathscr N_Y\to\mathscr N_X$, whose evaluations are $Rf_n^!$ and whose transitions are exactly the displayed mate formula. The unit and counit of $F_f\dashv\mathcal E_f$ are the restrictions of the ambient system unit and counit, so their triangle identities hold as equations of system morphisms. This argument uses invertibility of each displayed transition, not the bounded-below normalization clause of the system-adjoint theorem, so it applies without uniform bounds in the index.

source.place: Finite duality, coefficient-change compatibility, and enriched adjunction before total inverse limits.

proof.text: For each structure map $a_W:W\to\operatorname{Spec}k$, apply the same construction to the normalized coefficient-unit system. Nagata compactification supplies the required compactification, and the evaluated level is $Ra_{W,n}^!A_n=\omega_{W,n}$. Define $\Omega_W=\mathcal E_{a_W}((A_n)_{\operatorname{Spec}k})_n$ with the actual mate transitions. The finite dualizing comparison identifies these transitions with the counit-defined coefficient comparisons, and the integral dualizing proposition identifies $\mathcal L_W\Omega_W$ with the prescribed total-limit dualizing object, with the same finite projections. Choose $d_W\ge0$ with $\dim W\le d_W$ by finite-type dimension finiteness (take $d_W=0$ if empty), as required by the integral dualizing proposition.

source.place: Finite duality, coefficient-change compatibility, and enriched adjunction before total inverse limits.

proof.text: Define $\mathcal D_WM=\mathcal I_W(M,\Omega_W)$ using the system internal-Hom construction. Its level is $D_{W,n}M_n$. Finite Verdier preservation gives bounded constructibility and finite Tor amplitude; [cor-coef-finite-verdier] identifies its normalization map with the evaluation-defined isomorphism $T(D_{W,m}M_m)\cong D_{W,n}(TM_m)\cong D_{W,n}M_n$. The site comparison preserves these evaluation pairings. Exact levelwise inverse image defines $f^*$ on systems and commutes with derived coefficient extension, so it preserves normalization; [lem-sf-pullback-tor-amplitude] gives its finite-Tor constructibility. Thus $\mathcal D_W$ and $f^*$ act on the required normalized subcategories. Tensor also preserves these subcategories: its transitions are tensor products of the invertible input transitions, and its levelwise finite-Tor preservation is [lem-sf-tensor-ctf](ii).

source.place: Finite duality, coefficient-change compatibility, and enriched adjunction before total inverse limits.

proof.text:
Construct the compact-support composition map $\alpha:\mathcal F_{a_Y}\mathcal F_f\to\mathcal F_{a_X}$ from proper/open exchange and the direct-image and open-extension compositors on system resolutions. The ordinary system calculus constructs precisely these mate words. Their evaluations are the finite composition comparison [thm-sf-comp-composition], so $\alpha$ is an isomorphism on the normalized finite-Tor domain. For $K\in\mathscr N_X$ and $L\in\mathscr N_s$, composing the actual system adjunction bijections gives
$$\operatorname{Hom}_X(K,\mathcal E_f\mathcal E_{a_Y}L)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_s(\mathcal F_{a_Y}\mathcal F_fK,L)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_s(\mathcal F_{a_X}K,L)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_X(K,\mathcal E_{a_X}L).$$
Yoneda gives the counit-compatible isomorphism of these two system right adjoints. At the unit it is $c:\mathcal E_f\Omega_Y\cong\Omega_X$. Thus this comparison is constructed using Hom sets in the derived SYSTEM category. The finite composition theorem applies at each level since those complexes are bounded below and of etale origin; a uniform bound on systems is unnecessary.

source.place: Finite duality, coefficient-change compatibility, and enriched adjunction before total inverse limits.

proof.text:
Put $P=\mathcal D_YN$. Construct $\Pi:\mathcal F_f\mathcal E_fN\otimes^LP\to\mathcal F_f(\mathcal E_fN\otimes^Lf^*P)$ as the proper counit projection followed by the open tensor comparison on systems. Its evaluations are the projection maps of [fix-prop-projection-formula], with $K=Rf_n^!N_n\in D^b_c$ and $P_n\in D^b_{ctf}$, hence are invertible; therefore $\Pi$ is invertible. Form the actual system map
$$\mathcal F_f(\mathcal E_fN\otimes^Lf^*P)\xrightarrow{\Pi^{-1}}\mathcal F_f\mathcal E_fN\otimes^LP\xrightarrow{\epsilon_N\otimes1}N\otimes^LP\xrightarrow{\mathrm{ev}}\Omega_Y.$$
Transpose under the already constructed system adjunction $\mathcal F_f\dashv\mathcal E_f$ and compose with $c:\mathcal E_f\Omega_Y\cong\Omega_X$. Tensor-Hom transposition gives a natural system morphism
$$\theta_N:\mathcal E_fN\longrightarrow\mathcal I_X(f^*\mathcal D_YN,\Omega_X)=\mathcal D_Xf^*\mathcal D_YN.$$
Every arrow exists before evaluation. No system adjunction for the dual expression has been assumed.

source.place: Finite duality, coefficient-change compatibility, and enriched adjunction before total inverse limits.

proof.text:
To check invertibility of this particular $\theta$, work at level $n$ on the etale site. The internal adjunction at $\omega_Y$, using $f_n^\times\omega_Y\cong\omega_X$, gives $Rf_*D_XK\cong D_YRf_!K$. Biduality, ordinary pullback/direct-image adjunction and this comparison give
$$\operatorname{Hom}_X(K,D_Xf^*D_YN)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_X(f^*D_YN,D_XK)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_Y(D_YN,Rf_*D_XK)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_Y(D_YN,D_YRf_!K)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_Y(Rf_!K,N).$$
All objects to which biduality is applied are finite-Tor constructible by the preceding preservation steps. Under these bijections, postcomposition by $\theta_{N,n}$ corresponds to the adjunction bijection $h\mapsto\epsilon_N F_f(h)$: [lem-asd-internal-adjunction-evaluation] explicitly identifies the internal-adjunction transpose with projection, evaluation and the exceptional counit, exactly the composite defining $\theta$. Hence postcomposition by $\theta_{N,n}$ is bijective for every such $K$, and Yoneda makes $\theta_{N,n}$ invertible. The finite duality/site comparison identifies its pro-etale evaluation with this map. Conservativity now makes the already constructed SYSTEM map $\theta_N$ invertible. Its formula supplies the required evaluation/transpose identities on systems. This proves the dual formula without inferring a system adjunction from levelwise Hom bijections.

source.place: Finite duality, coefficient-change compatibility, and enriched adjunction before total inverse limits.

proof.text:
For the enriched assertion work first with the corresponding normalized etale systems $M,N$, using the equivalence of Step 5. Write $H=R\mathcal Hom_{A_\bullet}(M,G_f^{\mathrm{et}}N)$ and $Q=Rf_{*,\bullet}H$. The first input $M$ is normalized, so the system internal-Hom evaluation theorem applies even if $H$ or $Q$ is not normalized. We need projection for this arbitrary $Q$, rather than an unproved finite-Tor hypothesis on it. Construct
$$\Pi_{Q,M}:Q\otimes^LF_f^{\mathrm{et}}M\longrightarrow F_f^{\mathrm{et}}(f^*Q\otimes^LM)$$
as the proper counit projection followed by open tensor comparison. The ordinary system calculus supplies this transformation on all systems. Each evaluation is invertible by the UNBOUNDED proper projection theorem [lem-amb-proper-coproducts-projection] and open tensor theorem [lem-pur-etale-open-derived-tensor]. Thus this actual system projection map is invertible. No boundedness or normalization of $Q$ is needed.

source.place: Finite duality, coefficient-change compatibility, and enriched adjunction before total inverse limits.

proof.text:
Let $d_H:f^*Rf_{*,\bullet}H\to H$ be the ordinary direct-image counit and $e:H\otimes^LM\to G_f^{\mathrm{et}}N$ the internal-Hom evaluation. The following composite is an actual morphism of derived etale systems:
$$Q\otimes^LF_f^{\mathrm{et}}M\xrightarrow{\Pi_{Q,M}}F_f^{\mathrm{et}}(f^*Q\otimes^LM)\xrightarrow{F_f^{\mathrm{et}}(d_H\otimes1)}F_f^{\mathrm{et}}(H\otimes^LM)\xrightarrow{F_f^{\mathrm{et}}(e)}F_f^{\mathrm{et}}G_f^{\mathrm{et}}N\xrightarrow{\epsilon_N}N.$$
Transpose only under the closed tensor-Hom adjunction on the ringed SYSTEM topos. It defines
$$B_{M,N}:Rf_{*,\bullet}R\mathcal Hom(M,G_f^{\mathrm{et}}N)\longrightarrow R\mathcal Hom(F_f^{\mathrm{et}}M,N).$$
This construction uses $F_f^{\mathrm{et}}$ on actual morphisms and the actual exceptional counit. It never applies the Brown right adjoint to an internal mapping object or promotes an ordinary Hom-group bijection to a complex morphism. Functoriality of these displayed operations makes $B$ natural.

source.place: Finite duality, coefficient-change compatibility, and enriched adjunction before total inverse limits.

proof.text: Both first inputs $M$ and $F_f^{\mathrm{et}}M$ of the internal Homs are normalized, so evaluation identifies $B_{M,N}$ with the finite internal-adjunction map. The formula in [lem-asd-internal-adjunction-evaluation], with its test object equal to $Q_n$ and the identity map of $Q_n=Rf_*R\mathcal Hom(M_n,f_n^\times N_n)$, is exactly the evaluated composite of Step 15. Thus [prop-asd-internal-adjunction] makes every $e_nB$ invertible. Evaluations detect isomorphisms of derived systems, so $B$ is invertible there, with an inverse natural in $M,N$. Apply total termwise derived global sections and the derived direct-image composition isomorphism $R\Gamma_YRf_{*,\bullet}\cong R\Gamma_X$. This gives an actual isomorphism from $\mathcal H_X(M,\mathcal E_fN)$ to $\mathcal H_Y(\mathcal F_fM,N)$ on etale systems; define $\mathcal A_{M,N}$ to be its inverse. Its inverse identities are those of this actual isomorphism after applying a functor, not an inference that evaluations detect equality.

source.place: Finite duality, coefficient-change compatibility, and enriched adjunction before total inverse limits.

proof.text: Transport the preceding mapping-system isomorphism to the pro-etale realizations using actual comparison maps. The internal-Hom comparison is the transpose of comparison pullback applied to evaluation, constructed on systems by the tensor-Hom calculus. At every level its first input is finite-Tor constructible and its second is bounded constructible, so [lem-weil-finite-duality-site-comparison] makes it invertible. The unbounded comparison unit and derived direct-image composition identify its termwise global sections with the etale mapping system. These are isomorphisms of systems by evaluation conservativity. Together with the compact-support and exceptional comparison of Step 5 they transport $\mathcal A$ and its inverse as actual maps in $D(\operatorname{Tow}(\operatorname{Ab}))$. Their evaluation at $n$ is the inverse of the canonical internal-adjunction map followed by $R\Gamma$, hence exactly the displayed finite enriched adjunction. Its finite units and counits are those identified in Steps 4 and 7; the pairing formulas used to construct $B$ preserve the specified evaluation and transposition identities.

source.place: Finite duality, coefficient-change compatibility, and enriched adjunction before total inverse limits.

proof.text: The compact-support system transition is $F_mM_m\to F_m\operatorname{Res}_{m,n}M_n\cong\operatorname{Res}_{m,n}F_nM_n$; the restriction-of-scalars theorem identifies this with the specified finite quotient transition. Its scalar-extension adjoint is the normalization composite in Step 6. Consequently its total limit is the functor $\mathcal L_Y\mathcal F_f\mathcal R_X$ with the stated finite projections whenever integral compact support is defined in this way. Step 9 gives the dualizing total-limit identification. Applying total derived inverse limit to the actual mapping-system isomorphism and its inverse preserves their inverse identities and naturality. For $f=1$ the maps are the tensor-Hom evaluation transpose and biduality; zero inputs and empty source give zero systems, and $m=n$ gives the identity quotient map. No uniform bound or integral exceptional functor has been introduced.
